quests.title: Treasure Lost, Treasure Found

dialogue.t: Guizhong's Four Commandments... What are they really trying to tell us...
Haha, raring to go! That's what I like to see. Then let's begin our reading of Guizhong's Four Commandments.
"Teach with wisdom, be bound by virtue, fortify the bones, unite in ambition — the convergence of these four shall be known as the 'Guili Assembly.'"
On the surface, it does read like a set of commandments. Golden rules for life.
But it's also supposed to contain some sort of clues to a hidden treasure...
...I can't decipher it, though. It seems we'll have to approach this in what academics like to call the old-fashioned way...
Those seven passages we found previously, they were all located in ruins of some sort.
Since we're not sure where to start this time, perhaps keep searching in ruins for now.

dialogue.sit: Ruins of Liyue, here I come!

dialogue.t: Hmm... For now, let's limit the search area to Guili Plains.
However... as I'm just a scholar, there's no way I'd be able to keep up with you out in the field.
So I will leave the actual ruin-searching to you. Just let me know what you find.
While we're on the subject — I once came across a strange plate with some writing on in one of the ruins around here.
I only looked at it in isolation though. Didn't do any sort of holistic analysis.
Now I think about it, it might be connected to Guizhong's Four Commandments.
How about I mark the location on your map? You should go check it out, maybe it'll lead somewhere.
Just what exactly is being hidden in this saying...?
Though we call it a saying, it's really more of a riddle.
A riddle that has been kept alive by word of mouth among the residents of Guili Plains.
"At the place where wisdom and ambition, unity and fortitude converge like water; that is where I shall reveal the bountiful treasures of the earth."
How about that, eh? However you interpret it, it sure sounds like there's some kind of buried treasure in the Guili Plains area.
If I surmise correctly, those four words should correspond to four different ruins.
If one were to find all four ruins, perhaps they would be able to find the meaning behind this saying.
But I'm not cut out for finding all of them myself. Just finding that first one really took it out of me. Took days to recover.
If you're interested, perhaps you could take a look. Who knows, perhaps you'll find the next lead before I do.

If you're interested, perhaps you could take a look. Who knows, perhaps you'll find the next lead before I do.
I'll mark the first ruins I found on your map. I'd suggest starting there.
If you do find something, don't make the amateur mistake of running off in your excitement. Be sure to <color=#00E1FFFF>note down the clue</color> first.
Heading off? Well remember, if you come across anything exciting, don't forget to come back and tell me.
Unlikely. The great gods would not have waged an all-out war over a bit of treasure that took their fancy.
Or if they did, then you have to ask yourself... What kind of treasure would it take to drive the gods into war with each other?
...Haha, I for one cannot imagine such a treasure.

dialogue.sit: Maybe Guizhong and one of the other gods...

dialogue.t: Wh—What are you suggesting? ...You shouldn't pay any heed to those tall tales you hear in Liyue Harbor.
Guizhong was a god, a deity... Not a mere mortal...
...S—Surely a god wouldn't... Surely not...
Hey, there's some writing on this plate! ...But it's barely readable.
Paimon feels like it might have some special meaning.
I wonder how the Guili Assembly met its demise...
I wonder how the Guili Assembly met its demise...

dialogue.sit: Remind me of Guizhong's Four Commandments.

dialogue.t: Having trouble memorizing them? I understand, most people would. Fortunately, I have a rather good memory for this sort of thing.
Guizhong's Four Commandments are as follows: "Teach with wisdom, be bound by virtue, fortify the bones, unite in ambition — the convergence of these four shall be known as the 'Guili Assembly.'"

dialogue.sit: A battle for territory between the gods?

dialogue.t: A territorial challenge, you say? Hmm... but the Guili Assembly is said to have existed peacefully under Guizhong's rule for a very long time.
Not that Guizhong was a particularly powerful god... At least, that's my impression...
But there seems to have been another god with the Guili Assembly besides Guizhong. I highly doubt anyone would have been foolish enough to try and take on two gods at once...
Maybe it's to do with the Archon War.
A protracted war erupted between the gods, each of whom coveted a seat at one of the seven divine thrones in Celestia.
It seems that none in Teyvat escaped the reach of that all-consuming war.
Goodbye. Don't forget to come back and tell me if you find anything.
Sometimes fate is inescapable, even for a god...

dialogue.sit: I found four clues in four ruins.

dialogue.t: Four ruins, four clues... And there are Four Commandments.
Each of these clues expounds upon the meaning of one of the Four Commandments.
To get to the correct interpretation, the original text of Guizhong's Four Commandments is key. These four are helpful, but peripheral to our enquiry.
These five passages are all linked — but how?
Hmm... Could "convergence" mean that... these four things all link up in some way?
Wait — I remember, each of Guizhong's Four Commandments can be found in a specific ruin...
Hmm... I am speculating here, but perhaps the four <color=#00E1FFFF>ruins</color> are relevant to deciphering the true meaning of Guizhong's Four Commandments...
How exactly, I don't know. I need to mull it over. Maybe you could have a think too — or better still, go and investigate it firsthand.
I'm just a skinny little scholar after all, I tire out completely after a few seconds on the run... Wish I had your stamina!
Anyway, I'm going to keep thinking about it for a while. If you think of anything, or if you find anything, you know where I am.
It's a speculative hypothesis, but I believe the four ruins corresponding to each of Guizhong's Four Commandments may be relevant to deciphering their true meaning...
Exactly what role the ruins are supposed to play, well, that's another question. And... I don't think I have the physical strength to test out each of my hypotheses in full...
It's also possible that I just have a one-track mind, and this idea is leading me nowhere...
Did you find the treasure?
Did you find the treasure?
Did you find the treasure?
Did you find the treasure?
How is the search going? Found the treasure yet?

dialogue.sit: Yes, it was about where they "converge" after all.

dialogue.t: Really... So it's just like Guizhong's Four Commandments says. The treasure was located at "the convergence of these four..."
Whoever designed this riddle must have truly revered Guizhong.
So much so that they preserved Guizhong's Four Commandments for future generations, even though the Guili Assembly was wiped out.
And as for Guizhong herself, who established the commandments — she must have been adored by her people.

Clearly, she wished for her people to be wise, to hold themselves to a moral code, to be strong and healthy, and to find solidarity in the shared enterprise of protecting their home — the Guili Assembly...

dialogue.sit: I wish I could meet her...

dialogue.t: Failed? I suppose you're right, she died in the end... and when the Guili Assembly was wiped out, her people no longer had a place to call home.
And yet, today, Guizhong's Four Commandments have seen the light of day once more.
These were the words penned by Guizhong herself to serve both as maxims and blessing for her people.
Once there was a time when she led her people to go forth and take this very land, guided by these commandments.
She may no longer be with us, but her beliefs, the things she stood for — they will endure.
Whoever it was that revered her so much was very clever indeed. They used the allure of hidden treasure to ensure Guizhong's Four Commandments would be passed down.
Though for that person, I wonder whether the treasure they held dear was the rare metals and precious stones, or Guizhong's Four Commandments themselves.
Haha, well, to me at least, it's clear that the commandments are the real treasures here. A chest full of gold or gems can't compare.
...But if you made people choose, how many would really pick a list of commandments over material wealth?

quests.description: What secret does this set of archaic admonishments hold?
